name: Process Plant
description: Process plant diagrams: P&IDs and process flow diagrams in ISO 10628 (ISA-5.1 and ISO 14617 one choice away), instrument loop diagrams, HVAC flow diagrams, plumbing risers and piping isometrics. Element types follow the DEXPI class names; lines, loops and equipment are numbered from the project's tag formats.

rules.description: Instrument letters read as ISA-5.1 identification letters and start with the loop's variable.
Each instrument tag is used once.
Each equipment tag is used once.
Each line number is used once.
Each loop number is used once (within its variable when numbering is parallel).
Every off-page connector has a partner with the same tag.
rules.reference: ISO 10628-1, continuation arrows; PIP PIC001, off-page connectors

rules.description: Every signal off-page connector has a partner with the same tag.
rules.reference: ISO 10628-1, continuation arrows; PIP PIC001, off-page connectors

rules.description: Off-page partners sit on different sheets and carry the same line.
Every nozzle, valve and fitting port is connected or capped.
A control loop has a measuring element and a final element reachable along its signal lines.
Every instrument belongs to a loop.
A loop diagram shows one whole loop, every terminal landed both sides and each I/O channel once.
Every line has a size, a fluid and a piping class.
Every relief valve shows its set pressure and sizes.
Design pressure is at least operating pressure.
Pipes join piping nodes and signal lines join instruments, as the connection table allows.
rules.reference: ANSI/ISA-5.1, instrument lines; ISO 10628-1, flow lines

rules.description: Every stream of a process flow diagram is numbered.
Every duct run has a size and an airflow.
Every fixture has its fixture units and its system.
Each page shows only what its kind of diagram holds.

examples.label: P&ID: feed drum level control
